blocks.text: Micro-organisms are tiny living things that can only be seen with a microscope. They play significant roles in our environment, health, and industry.

blocks.markdown: Micro-organisms are classified into four main groups: **Bacteria**, **Viruses**, **Fungi**, and **Protozoa**. Each group has unique characteristics and functions in various habitats, including aquatic and terrestrial environments.

blocks.title: Definition of Micro-organisms
blocks.text: Micro-organisms are microscopic organisms that exist as unicellular (single-celled) or multicellular (many-celled) entities.

blocks.markdown:
### Useful and Harmful Micro-organisms
- **Bacteria**: Useful examples include *Lactobacillus* used in yogurt production, while harmful examples include *Escherichia coli* which can cause food poisoning.
- **Viruses**: Some viruses such as the *Bacteriophage* can kill harmful bacteria, while others like the *HIV* virus can cause diseases.
- **Fungi**: Useful fungi include *Penicillium*, which is used to produce antibiotics, whereas harmful fungi like *Aspergillus* can cause infections.
- **Protozoa**: Certain protozoa like *Amoeba* are beneficial in nutrient cycling, while others like *Plasmodium* cause malaria.

blocks.title: Identifying Micro-organisms
blocks.prompt: Classify the following micro-organisms into useful or harmful categories: *Lactobacillus*, *HIV*, *Penicillium*, *Plasmodium*.

steps.text: Identify *Lactobacillus* as a useful bacterium used in yogurt production.
Recognize *HIV* as a harmful virus that causes AIDS.
Classify *Penicillium* as a useful fungus that produces antibiotics.
Identify *Plasmodium* as a harmful protozoan that causes malaria.

blocks.markdown:
### Controlling Harmful Micro-organisms
One effective method of controlling harmful micro-organisms is through **sanitation**. This includes practices like regular handwashing, proper food handling, and maintaining clean environments to prevent the spread of diseases.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember to clearly differentiate between useful and harmful micro-organisms in your answers. Use examples to support your points.

points: Micro-organisms are classified into four main groups: bacteria, viruses, fungi, and protozoa.
Understanding the roles of micro-organisms helps in identifying their benefits and risks to human health.
